articles.summary: The cost of AI infrastructure goes beyond GPUs and API bills. Every vector database, search cluster, cache, and pipeline wrapped around the model adds network hops, failure modes, data to keep in sync, and systems to debug. What the distributed AI stack costs in latency, reliability, and engineering time, and which capabilities can run inside the application as an embedded AI runtime instead.
articles.title: The Hidden Cost of AI Infrastructure

articles.summary: Casuro's VOCAL is a voice AI agent that interviews candidates on a company's job page. How Casuro uses Moss for sub-10ms retrieval of candidate and job context as it scales toward thousands of concurrent conversations.
articles.title: How Casuro Built a Production Voice AI Interviewer with Moss

articles.summary: OpenMOSS and Moss at Moss.dev share a name but build different parts of the AI stack. OpenMOSS releases open-weight generative models like MOSS-Image; Moss builds sub-10ms semantic search and retrieval infrastructure for voice agents and real-time AI.
articles.title: OpenMOSS vs. Moss.dev: What's the Difference?

articles.summary: Cloud, edge, on-device, or browser AI? Each place an AI application can run trades latency, privacy, offline use, and model size differently. Why voice agents feel every network hop, where each component belongs, and how running retrieval inside the agent's own process removes a trip from every conversational turn.
articles.title: Run AI Where Your Users Are: Browser, Edge, Device, or Cloud
